about: Whether a programme can be replayed at a given moment.
notes: Arguments are the programme, the channel's catch-up days, and the current time in Unix milliseconds. Fixing 'now' is what makes this answerable as data.

All three conditions must hold: the channel keeps an archive, the programme has finished, and it began inside the window. Offering a replay the panel will refuse spends a connection to learn what the listing already said.

cases.name: a programme that finished an hour ago, on a channel with a week
the same programme, on a channel with no archive
a programme still on air cannot be replayed
cases.why: It is live, and the two must never both be true for one programme.

cases.name: a programme that has not started cannot be replayed
a programme older than the window cannot be replayed
a programme that began exactly at the edge of the window still can
cases.why: The boundary is inclusive, so a listing and a replay agree about the oldest programme on offer.

cases.name: a programme that ends exactly now is replayable
cases.why: The instant it ends it is over. This boundary is the counterpart of the one in isOnNow, which requires endsAt > now: at that single instant the programme is neither on air nor unavailable, and the two never overlap. A second implementation choosing >= in either place would make one programme both live and catch-up.
